bug_semantics: In Apache Cassandra 5.0 mTLS (MutualTlsAuthenticator), ADD IDENTITY maps a client-certificate identity onto a role used for authentication. AddIdentityStatement.authorize() checked Permission.CREATE on the caller's own primary role (state.getUser().getPrimaryRole()) and never inspected the target role. execute() then called RoleManager.addIdentity(identity, role) with the CQL-supplied role and no further authorization. A user granted CREATE on roles (for example GRANT CREATE ON ALL ROLES, which satisfies CREATE on the caller's primary role) could therefore bind their certificate identity to an arbitrary existing role, including a superuser such as cassandra, and then authenticate as that role. The same first-write also left DROP IDENTITY checking DROP only on the caller's primary role. CreateRoleStatement in the same tree already required CREATE on RoleResource.root() and forbade non-superusers from creating superuser roles; ADD IDENTITY omitted both controls.
flaw_origin: The unsafe ADD IDENTITY authorization was written as part of the CASSANDRA-18554 mTLS authenticator feature, not by a later edit. f078c02cb58bddd735490b07548f7352f0eb09aa first added AddIdentityStatement.java with authorize() at lines 51-55 calling checkPermission(state, Permission.CREATE, state.getUser().getPrimaryRole()). The parent tree 192a639088c94ad820bb7475d3970d705c101e67 has no AddIdentityStatement, no DROP IDENTITY, and no ADD IDENTITY grammar. git log -L / -S / blame show that line unchanged until the CASSANDRA-21219 fix. The contemporaneous CQL doc said only users with privileges to add roles may add identities, matching CreateRoleStatement's RoleResource.root() check, so the first-write used the wrong permission resource and skipped the superuser-binding guard.
